text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.

- European intelligence agencies discovered 40 artilery pieces smuggled into Bosnia in late August through Croatian port Ploce, the New York Times repors. Turkey and Malaysia thought to have played a role in the operation.
- Insurer Addenda introduces an additional private health policy at 59 and 135 kuna per month to provide better care.
- Croatian bourse warns some companies are slow to transfer titles of shares. Confectioner Kras and food processor Podravka, whose shares are among the most popular, outlined as typical examples.
- Money market rate dropped 89 basis points last week, reversing the previous trend as stable liquidity prevails.
- Croatia has 267,619 jobless, or 9.5 more than a year ago, according to state statistics.
- Prices of some oil derivatives, excluding petrol, rose between 12.8 and 32.1 percent on Tuesday, natural gas went up to 75 from 68 kuna per cubic meter.

- Foreign investors, confused by frequent legal changes and different interpretations of laws, are still holding back from larger investments in Croatia, says Stephen Revell of the British law firm Freshfields.
- Stock market is recovering at a cautious but stable pace, analysts say. Hoteliers were again amongst the most actively traded issues in the past week.
- Austria's Raiffeisenbank will be the first foreign bank in Croatia some in three weeks to extend loans to citizens for housing and car purchases, board chairman Zdenko Adrovic says.
- While average Croatian profit rate in the first six months reached 26.8 percent, in Split-Dalmatia county it was only 6.5 percent as exports dropped and shipbuilders registered substantial losses.
- South Korea's Samsung to invest $34.5 million in modernisation of the main Adriatic port in Rijeka to increase its capacity to 10 million tonnes of goods per year.
- Stock market turnover increased by 58 percent in the past week with 83,025 shares sold. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
